co-cultivation of fungi isolated from the same host organism can activate new secondary metabolites and deactivate existing secondary metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-cultivation of fungi isolated from the same source is an effective strategy to activate transcription of otherwise silent gene clusters.
co-cultivation is a valuable strategy for activating otherwise transcriptionally silent metabolites, and for revealing the complexity of the chemical warfare that occurs during fungal co-culture.

co-cultivation can be a useful approach for the discovery of novel secondary metabolites, especially when the strains are derived from a natural environment where they are likely to be in contact with each other, and that it can be used as a tool to understand how the secondary metabolites are regulated in a natural context.
